{{nihongo|'''Sato Shrine (Hitachiota)'''|薩都神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|Q134917287|qid=Q134917287}}, and under the former {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}} its rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* '''Tachihayabi-no-Mikoto''' (たちはやびおのみこと)

This deity appears in the {{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11481687|qid=Q11481687}} as an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=amatsukami}}. The text says: "His name is '''Tachihayao-no-Mikoto'''; another name is '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hayafuwake-no-Mikoto}}'''." In the fudoki, when local residents suffered from the deity's curse, Kataoka no Ōmuraji (grandson of {{ill|Kuninazu no Ōkashima no Mikoto|Q99517269|qid=Q99517269}}), ancestor of the Kashima branch of the Nakatomi clan ({{ill|Nakatomi no Kashima no Muraji|Q11677139|qid=Q11677139|lt=Nakatomi no Kashima no Muraji}}), was dispatched by the court to perform rites.

=== History ===
=== Foundation ===
The {{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11481687|qid=Q11481687}} contains an entry on Sato Shrine and states that the founding was in {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 7 ({{ill|788|Q30721|qid=Q30721}}), when a shrine was built in Matsuzawa. In Enryaku 19 ({{ill|800|Q23677|qid=Q23677}}), villagers petitioned and a great minister was dispatched; an oracle said, "Rather than dwell in an impure village, settle in the pure heights." The shrine was moved to Kabire-no-mine (Iriyonoma-chō, {{ill|Hitachi, Ibaraki|Q633922|qid=Q633922}}). In {{ill|Daidō|de|Daidō (Ära)|es|Daidō|fa|دایدو (دوره)|fr|Ère Daidō|ia|Daido|id|Daidō|ja|大同 (日本)|ko|다이도 (일본)|ru|Дайдо (нэнго)|simple|Daidō|sr|Даидо|th|ไดโด|tr|Daidō|uk|Дайдо|zh|大同 (日本)|zh_yue|大同 (日本)|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} 1 ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}), because the mountain was steep and worship difficult, it was moved again to Konakajima (Satonomiya-chō, {{ill|Hitachiōta, Ibaraki|Q838663|qid=Q838663}}).

The first appearance in official histories ({{ill|National Histories|Q11420601|qid=Q11420601}}) is in the entry for {{ill|September 8|Q2850|qid=Q2850}} of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 13 ({{ill|846|Q30454|qid=Q30454}}) in the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}, where Sato deity of 10th merit rank is granted Junior Fifth Rank, Lower. It continued to rise, reaching Junior Fourth Rank, Lower in {{ill|Jōgan|de|Jōgan|es|Jōgan|fa|جوگان|fr|Ère Jōgan|ia|Jogan|id|Jōgan|ja|貞観 (日本)|ko|조간 (연호)|ru|Дзёган|simple|Jōgan|sr|Џоган|tr|Jōgan|uk|Дзьоґан (ненґо)|zh|貞觀 (日本)|zh_yue|貞觀 (日本)|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 16 ({{ill|874|Q23843|qid=Q23843}}). In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as a small shrine in {{ill|Kuji District, Ibaraki|Q1075212|qid=Q1075212}}, {{ill|Hitachi Province|Q1055353|qid=Q1055353}}. At the end of the Six National Histories period, its divine rank was higher than {{ill|Shizu Shrine|Q11663648|qid=Q11663648}}, the district's {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}, but in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} it is listed as a small shrine, suggesting their relative influence reversed during that interval.

From the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} onward it was revered by the {{ill|Satake clan|Q2975363|qid=Q2975363}}. According to this shrine's origin record, {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|Q11383430|qid=Q11383430|lt=Satake Yoshinobu}} repaired the buildings in the {{ill|Shōhei|Q1143587|qid=Q1143587|lt=Shōhei}} era, and shrine tradition says {{ill|Satake Yoshikiyo|Q11383467|qid=Q11383467}} moved it to the current location in {{ill|Daiei (era)|Q1193564|qid=Q1193564}} 2 ({{ill|1522|Q6299|qid=Q6299}}).

In June of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Divine ranks ===
* {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 13 ({{ill|846|Q30454|qid=Q30454}}), {{ill|September 8|Q2850|qid=Q2850}}: from 10th merit rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower, 10th merit rank ({{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}) - written as "Sato deity".
* {{ill|Jōgan|de|Jōgan|es|Jōgan|fa|جوگان|fr|Ère Jōgan|ia|Jogan|id|Jōgan|ja|貞観 (日本)|ko|조간 (연호)|ru|Дзёган|simple|Jōgan|sr|Џоган|tr|Jōgan|uk|Дзьоґан (ненґо)|zh|貞觀 (日本)|zh_yue|貞觀 (日本)|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 8 ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), {{ill|May 27|Q2587|qid=Q2587}}: from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper, 7th merit rank to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper, 7th merit rank ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}) - written as "Sato deity".
* Jōgan 16 ({{ill|874|Q23843|qid=Q23843}}), {{ill|December 29|Q2862|qid=Q2862}}: from Senior Fifth Rank, Upper, 7th merit rank to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower, 7th merit rank (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') - written as "Sato deity".
